title: Counit-normalized descent of the ordinary integral completion map
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] set $C_{W,n}=(R/t^n)_W$ for $n\geq1$, $B_W=\varprojlim_n C_{W,n}$, with quotient projections $\pi_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $c_f:f^{-1}B_Y\to B_X$ be the adjoint of the limit map $B_Y\to f_*B_X$ whose $n$-th projection is the constant-section map after $\pi_{Y,n}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use module sheaves, sheaf tensor and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $f_B^*M=B_X\otimes_{f^{-1}B_Y}f^{-1}M$, with its ordinary module adjunction [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction].

Let $q_W$ denote localization of cochain complexes in $D(B_W)$, and let $P_f=Lf_B^*$ with its canonical computation counit $\epsilon_Q:P_f(q_YQ)\to q_X(f_B^*Q)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Let $\mathcal G_Y$ be the full category of flat-term K-flat cochain complexes [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. For $Q\in\mathcal G_Y$ form the strict tower $T_f(Q)_n=\operatorname{Res}_{\pi_{X,n}}f_n^*(Q\otimes_{B_Y}C_{Y,n})$ with its actual quotient transitions, and put $H_f(Q)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-derived-limit]. Write $\lambda_Q:\widehat P_f(q_YQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}q_XH_f(Q)$ for the canonical representative comparison of the completed pullback [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Let $\alpha_Q:f_B^*Q\to H_f(Q)$ be the chain map with quotient-generator formula $b\otimes q\mapsto1\otimes(q\otimes\pi_{X,n}(b))$ in every unshifted product projection and zero shifted product coordinate [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction].

There exists a unique natural transformation $\eta:P_f\to\widehat P_f$ such that for every $Q\in\mathcal G_Y$ the following equality holds in $D(B_X)$:
$$\lambda_Q\circ\eta_{q_YQ}=q_X(\alpha_Q)\circ\epsilon_Q.$$
For every quasi-isomorphism $p:Q\to A$ with $Q\in\mathcal G_Y$, its component on $q_YA$ is exactly
$$\eta_{q_YA}=\widehat P_f(q_Yp)\circ\lambda_Q^{-1}\circ q_X(\alpha_Q)\circ\epsilon_Q\circ P_f(q_Yp)^{-1}.$$
These formulas agree for all such resolutions under the canonical comparisons and for morphisms represented by roofs of quasi-isomorphisms between good complexes. The strict zero shifted-product coordinate is retained in the normalization. This statement asserts a morphism on arbitrary ambient derived objects; it makes no assertion that $P_f$ preserves constructibility or that $\eta$ is invertible.

proof.text: Work in a common universe in which the small pro-etale sites are small relative to the module categories. Let $\mathcal P_Y$ be the full subcategory of the homotopy category on the flat-term K-flat complexes, let $W$ be its quasi-isomorphisms, and write $L:\mathcal P_Y\to D(B_Y)$ for the restriction of localization. The resolving-class theorem identifies $\mathcal P_Y[W^{-1}]\to D(B_Y)$ as an equivalence, so $L$ is a localization at $W$ (compose the localization universal property with this equivalence). Every complex $A$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $Q\to A$ with $Q$ in this class by the K-flat resolution theorem. These assertions apply to the actual sheaf of rings $B_Y$; they do not require it to be a constant discrete ring or impose boundedness on $A$.

proof.text: Apply the strict quotient augmentation theorem to the ring map $c_f$ and to the actual quotient transitions specified in the statement. It gives the chain map $\alpha_Q=(a_Q,0)$ and, for every chain map $v:Q\to Q'$, the equality $H_f(v)\alpha_Q=\alpha_{Q'}f_B^*(v)$ as chain maps. In particular the second coordinate is zero in this equality, not merely invisible under the projections to the unshifted product. Restrict this natural chain map to the good complexes. No completeness or constructibility hypothesis on $Q$ is used.

proof.text:
For each good $Q$ set $\gamma_Q=\lambda_Q^{-1}q_X(\alpha_Q)\epsilon_Q$. The ordinary derived-pullback theorem provides the natural canonical counit $\epsilon$, and the well-definedness theorem for completed operations provides the natural representative isomorphism $\lambda$. For a chain map $v:Q\to Q'$ between good complexes their naturality and Step 2 give
$$q_X(f_B^*v)\epsilon_Q=\epsilon_{Q'}P_f(q_Yv),\qquad q_XH_f(v)\lambda_Q=\lambda_{Q'}\widehat P_f(q_Yv),$$
$$q_XH_f(v)q_X\alpha_Q=q_X\alpha_{Q'}q_X(f_B^*v).$$
Substitution and cancellation of $\lambda_{Q'}$ yield $\widehat P_f(q_Yv)\gamma_Q=\gamma_{Q'}P_f(q_Yv)$. Every morphism of $\mathcal P_Y$ is represented by such a chain map. Since $q_Yv$ depends only on its homotopy class, the displayed equality proves that $\gamma$ is a natural transformation $P_fL\to\widehat P_fL$ on $\mathcal P_Y$. Thus no choice of a homotopy representative affects this assertion.

proof.text: Both functors $P_fL$ and $\widehat P_fL$ invert $W$, since $L$ does and they are functors on $D(B_Y)$. Apply the natural-transformation part of the localization universal property to the localization $L$ established in Step 1, with these two functors, their existing lifts $P_f,\widehat P_f$, and identity lifting comparisons. It gives a unique natural transformation $\eta:P_f\to\widehat P_f$ whose restriction is $\gamma$. On a good $Q$ this says $\eta_{q_YQ}=\lambda_Q^{-1}q_X(\alpha_Q)\epsilon_Q$, and multiplication by $\lambda_Q$ is precisely the required counit-normalized equality.

proof.text: If $\eta'$ satisfies the prescribed equality, cancellation of the isomorphism $\lambda_Q$ gives $\eta'_{q_YQ}=\gamma_Q$ for every good $Q$. The faithfulness assertion for natural transformations under restriction along the localization $L$ then gives $\eta'=\eta$. In particular uniqueness concerns the actual canonical counit and the chosen representative comparison; it does not permit replacing either by a conjugate comparison.

proof.text:
For any quasi-isomorphism $p:Q\to A$ with $Q$ good, $q_Yp$ is invertible. Naturality of the transformation constructed in Step 4 gives
$$\eta_{q_YA}P_f(q_Yp)=\widehat P_f(q_Yp)\eta_{q_YQ}.$$
Multiply on the right by $P_f(q_Yp)^{-1}$ and insert the good-complex formula from Step 4. The result is exactly
$$\eta_{q_YA}=\widehat P_f(q_Yp)\lambda_Q^{-1}q_X(\alpha_Q)\epsilon_QP_f(q_Yp)^{-1}.$$
If $p':Q'\to A$ is another resolution, its expression also equals this same component $\eta_{q_YA}$. More explicitly, for the canonical derived comparison $u=(q_Yp')^{-1}q_Yp$, naturality gives $\widehat P_f(u)\gamma_Q=\gamma_{Q'}P_f(u)$; hence the two displayed resolution expressions agree under the canonical comparisons.

source.place: Tags 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization), 04VK (right localization); natural-transformation universal property as stated by lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property, with Mathlib CategoryTheory.Localization.fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft and liftNatTrans (Predicate.lean:278,326).

proof.text:
For a roof $Q\xleftarrow{s}R\xrightarrow{v}Q'$ between good complexes, with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism, put $h=(q_Yv)(q_Ys)^{-1}$. Naturality on its two arrows yields
$$\widehat P_f(q_Yv)\gamma_R=\gamma_{Q'}P_f(q_Yv),\qquad \widehat P_f(q_Ys)\gamma_R=\gamma_QP_f(q_Ys).$$
Invert the functor images of $q_Ys$ in the second equality and substitute into the first to obtain $\widehat P_f(h)\gamma_Q=\gamma_{Q'}P_f(h)$. Thus the formulas are compatible with roofs, including changes of a roof representing the same derived morphism. The restriction of $\eta$ is still represented by the original $(a_Q,0)$ after the specified counit and $\lambda_Q$; descent introduced no nonzero shifted coordinate. None of these cancellations asserts that $\eta$ is invertible or that ordinary pullback preserves constructibility.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryIntegralCompletionComparison_existsUnique :
    ∃! η : ordinaryIntegralDerivedPull l E f ⟶ integralDerivedPullback l E f,
      ∀ P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory,
        η.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≫
            (integralDerivedPullbackComparison l E f).hom.app P =
          ordinaryIntegralPullComplexCounit l E f P.obj ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map (ordinaryIntegralCompletionChain l E f P.obj)
lean.note: Existing public theorem at the exact source place named by this node. Its unique natural transformation has the stated normalization using the actual ordinary cochain counit and strict (quotients, zero) Roos chain map. Naturality and inversion of the localized resolution arrow give the displayed arbitrary-resolution formula, independence of resolution, and compatibility with roofs; see report for the equations. The theorem is valid for every scheme morphism, so specializes to schemes where l is invertible (the more-general-existing-theorem ruling). It asserts neither constructibility nor invertibility of eta. No construction or theorem is restated.
